questions.question: The Shevaroy Hills are located in which state of India?
questions.questionHtml: The Shevaroy Hills are located in which state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu. 

Key Points

  • The Shevaroy Hills is a mountain range located in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu.
  • It is situated near the town of Yercaud, which is a popular tourist destination known for its scenic beauty and pleasant weather.
  • The Shevaroy Hills are home to a variety of flora and fauna, including several rare and endangered species of plants and animals.
  • The hills are also known for their coffee and spice plantations, which are a major source of livelihood for the local communities.

Additional Information

  • The Eastern Ghats run almost parallel to the east coast of India leaving broad plains between their base and the coast.
  • It is a chain of highly broken and detached hills starting from the Mahanadi in Odisha to the Vagai in Tamil Nadu.
  • They almost disappear between the Godavari and the Krishna.
  • The Eastern Ghats reappear as more or less a continuous hill range in Cuddapah and Kurnool districts of Andhra Pradesh where they are called as Nallamala Range with a general elevation of 600-850 m.
    • Located south of the Krishna River, the hills run north to south, parallel to the Coromandel Coast on the Bay of Bengal.
    • The rugged, sparsely populated hills are composed for the most part of jumbled quartzites and slates and exemplify the mountain scenery of the Eastern Ghats.
  • The southern part of this range is called the Palkonda range.
    • The hills trend northwest to southeast and form the central part of the Eastern Ghats.
    • Geologically, they are relicts of ancient mountains formed during the Cambrian Period that were subsequently eroded by the Penneru River and its tributaries.
  • Javadi Hills, range of hills, one of the larger of the Eastern Ghats, in northern Tamil Nadu state, southeastern India.
    • Their steep southeastern flanks are forested with sandalwood.
    • The hills are sparsely populated.
    • Grains, legumes, and oilseeds are the chief crops.

questions.question: In India Who among the following has the power to pardon, reprieve or commute the punishment of any criminal?
questions.questionHtml: In India Who among the following has the power to pardon, reprieve or commute the punishment of any criminal?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is PresidentKey PointsPardoning Power of President

  • Article 72 empowers the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence.
  • The meaning of these terms is as follows:
    • Pardon: It removes both the sentence and the conviction and completely absolves the convict from all sentences, punishments, and disqualifications.
    • Commutation: It denotes the substitution of one form of punishment with a lighter form of punishment. For example, a death sentence may be commuted to rigorous imprisonment.
    • Remission: It implies reducing the period of the sentence without changing its character. For example, a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for five years may be remitted to rigorous imprisonment for one year.
    • Respite: It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of one originally awarded due to some special fact, such as the physical disability of a convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender.
    • Reprieve: It implies a stay of the execution of a sentence (especially that of death) for a temporary period. Its purpose is to enable the convict to have time to seek pardon or commutation from the President.

questions.question: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
questions.questionHtml: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

Key Points

  • Nalacharitam is a play that originated in the state of Kerala, which is known for its rich cultural heritage and traditional dance forms.
  • Nalacharitham was written by Unnayi Warrier in the 18th century. 
  • The play Nalacharitam is a popular performance in Kathakali, which tells the story of King Nala and his struggles.​

Important Points

  • Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art is the folk dance form of Kerala.
  • It is a combination of 5 forms of fine art which are –
    • Natyam (expressions)
    • Nritham (dance)
    • Nrithyam (enactment) 
    • Sangeetam (music)
    • Vadya (instruments)
  • Various costumes of characters of Kathakali –
    • Sathwika (Hero)
    • Katti (Villain)
    • Minukku (females)
    • Thathi (other characters)
  • Types of Drums used in Kathakali – Maddalam, Chenda, and Idakka
  • Kathakali is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which actors speak ‘sign language’ where hand gestures are used to dictate word part of the character and facial and eye movements express emotions and mood.
  • Kathakali is based on the epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata. 

Additional Information

  • Kathak, on the other hand, is a classical dance form that originated in North India and is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements.
  • Sattriya is a classical dance form from the state of Assam.
  • Odissi is a classical dance form from the state of Odisha.

questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following pair of compound – melting point is correct?

I. Acetic acid – 290K

II. Ethanol – 156K
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

Key Points Ethanol

  • Ethanol is still a liquid at room temperature, and it has a melting point of 156 K and a boiling point of 351 K.
  • It is used as a preservative in paints because it is an efficient solvent and often used in cleaning materials to prevent breach of organisms.
  • It is used in gasoline to avoid piston knocking and to preserve driveability.
  • It is a strong, water-mixable solvent containing other organic solvents, including acetone, tetrachloride carbon, ethylene glycol, chloroform, benzene, diethyl alcohol, glycerol, pyridine, nitromethane, and toluene.

Acetic acid

  • Acetic acid is an organic compound that belongs to a group of acids called carboxylic acids.
  • The formula of acetic acid is CH3COOH with a methyl group is attached to a carboxyl functional group.
  • The melting point of acetic acid is 290 K or 16.5°C and hence it often freezes during winter in cold climates.
  • The IUPAC name of acetic acid is ethanoic acid. Acetic acid is the main component of vinegar.
  • 5-8% solution of acetic acid in water is called vinegar and is used widely as a preservative in pickles.
  • Vinegar's sour taste and pungent smell are due to the presence of acetic acid.
  • Uses of Acetic Acid:
    • Acetic acid is used in the production of a wide range of dyes, rayons, silk, and perfumes.
    • Acetic acid is also used in the production of rubber.
    • It is mostly used in a pickle preservative as vinegar.
    • It is injected directly into the tumour during cancer treatment.
  • Therefore Both I and II are correct.

  • The Fergusson College was developed from the New English School, which was founded in 1880 by four young men: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, and Madhavrao Namjoshi.

  • The Fergusson College was one of the first colleges in India to offer a liberal arts education.
  • It was also one of the first colleges to be established by Indians, and it quickly became a center of Indian nationalism.
  • The college's alumni include many prominent figures in Indian history, including Lokmanya Tilak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, and R.G. Bhandarkar.
  • The Fergusson College has continued to be a leading institution of higher education in India.
  • It is now a constituent college of the University of Pune, and it offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs.
  • The college is also home to a number of research centers and institutes, and it has produced many notable scholars and scientists.
  • The Fergusson College is a proud institution with a long and distinguished history.

  • It is a testament to the vision and dedication of its founders, and it continues to play an important role in the development of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Basavanna.

Key Points

  • The twelfth century witnessed the emergence of a new movement in Karnataka, led by a Brahmana named Basavanna (1106-68) who was a minister in the court of a Kalachuri ruler.
  • His followers were known as Virashaivas (heroes of Shiva) or Lingayats (wearers of the linga).

Additional Information

  • Lingayats continue to be an important community in the region to date.
  • They worship Shiva in his manifestation as a linga, and men usually wear a small linga in a silver case on a loop strung over the left shoulder.
  • Those who are revered include the jangama or wandering monks.
  • Lingayats believe that on death the devotee will be united with Shiva and will not return to this world.
  • Therefore they do not practise funerary rites such as cremation, prescribed in the Dharmashastras.
  • Instead, they ceremonially bury their dead.
  • The Lingayats challenged the idea of caste and the “pollution” attributed to certain groups by Brahmanas.
  • They also questioned the theory of rebirth.
  • These won them followers amongst those who were marginalised within the Brahmanical social order.
  • The Lingayats also encouraged certain practices disapproved in the Dharmashastras, such as post-puberty marriage and the remarriage of widows.

  • Our understanding of the Virashaiva tradition is derived from vachanas (literally, sayings) composed in Kannada by women and men who joined the movement.

questions.question: What happens to the guard cells when water flows into them?
questions.questionHtml: What happens to the guard cells when water flows into them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Stomatal pores open.

Key Points

  • Stomata are tiny pores present on the surface of the leaves.
  • Massive amounts of gaseous exchange take place in the leaves through these pores for the purpose of photosynthesis.
  • But it is important to note here that the exchange of gases occurs across the surface of stems, roots, and leaves as well.
  • Since large amounts of water can also be lost through these stomata, the plant closes these pores when it does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
  • The opening and closing of the pore is a function of the guard cells.
  • The guard cells swell when water flows into them, causing the stomatal pore to open. Similarly, the pore closes if the guard cells shrink.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true and R is false.

Key Points

Explanation:

Assertion (A): India did indeed have a surplus in its balance of trade during most of the British Raj.

  • This means that the value of its exports exceeded the value of its imports.
  • This was due to several factors, including:
    • Forced cultivation of cash crops: The British forced Indian farmers to grow crops like indigo and cotton for export, even if it meant neglecting food production for domestic consumption.
    • Deindustrialization: British policies destroyed India's traditional industries, making the country more dependent on imported manufactured goods.
    • Drain of wealth: A significant portion of the trade surplus was not reinvested in India, but sent back to Britain as tribute and profits for British companies.

Reason (R): However, the statement that the surplus of the balance of trade was used for the growth and development of India is false.

  • The benefits of the trade surplus primarily accrued to the British, while India suffered from:
    • Underdevelopment: The drain of wealth and focus on cash crops over food production stunted India's economic development and exacerbated poverty.
    • Exploitation: Indian farmers and laborers were often exploited by British companies and landowners, receiving meager wages and working in poor conditions.
    • Lack of infrastructure: Despite the trade surplus, the British invested very little in India's infrastructure, such as roads, railways, and education, which further hampered development.
 

Therefore, while it is true that India had a positive balance of trade under British rule, the surplus was not used for its growth and development, but rather benefited the British at the expense of the Indian people.

  • The Zeroth Law plainly states that when two systems A and B are in thermal equilibrium, there must be a physical quantity that has the same value for both.
  • Temperature is a thermodynamic variable whose value is the same for two systems in thermal equilibrium (T ).

Additional Information

questions.questionHtml: Which number among 11368, 11638, 11863 and 12638 is divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
Given:

The numbers = 11368, 11638, 11863 and 12638

Concept:

A number divided by 11only when the difference of the sum of the digits at odd positions and sum of the digits at even positions is zero of multiple of 11.

Calculation:

For number 11368

⇒ (1 + 3 + 8) - (1 + 6)

⇒ 12 - 7 = 5 

Not divisible by 11

For number 11638

⇒ (1 + 6 + 8) - (1 + 3)

⇒ 15 - 4 = 11

Number 11638 is divisible by 11

For number 11863

⇒ (1 + 8 + 3) - (1 + 6)

⇒ 12 - 7 = 5

This number is not divisible by 11

For number 12638

⇒ (1 + 6 + 8) - (2 + 3)

⇒ 15 - 5 = 10

This number is not divisible by 11

∴ The required result will be 11638.

 

Alternate Method

Let's apply this rule to each of the given numbers.

11368:

Odd position digits: 1, 3, 8

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 56 cm is 1408 cm 2 . Find the diameter of the base of the cylinder.
questions.questionHtml: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 56 cm is 1408 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the diameter of the base of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for Curved Surface Area (CSA) using Diameter (d): π × d × h = 1408

(22/7) × d × 56 = 1408

22 × d × 8 = 1408

176 × d = 1408

d = 1408 ÷ 176 = 8 cm = 0.08 m

∴ The correct answer is 0.08 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height (h) of the cylinder = 56 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 1408 cm2

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area of a right circular cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Where r is the radius and h is the height.

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 56 = 1408

⇒ 44 × r × (56 ÷ 7) = 1408

⇒ 44 × r × 8 = 1408

⇒ 352 × r = 1408

⇒ r = 1408 ÷ 352

⇒ r = 4 cm

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2 × r = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

⇒ In meters: d = 8 ÷ 100 m = 0.08 m

∴ The correct answer is 0.08 m.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = 2 × π × r × (h + r).

Volume of Cylinder

The space occupied by the cylinder is given by the formula: Volume = π × r2 × h.

To convert centimeters to meters, divide the value by 100 (1 m = 100 cm).

questions.question: The average of all prime numbers between 32 and 69 is:
questions.questionHtml: The average of all prime numbers between 32 and 69 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

List all prime numbers between 32 and 69: 37, 41, 43, 47, 53, 59, 61, 67.

Total count of prime numbers (n) = 8.

Sum using pairing: (37+67) + (41+61) + (43+59) + (47+53) = 104 + 102 + 102 + 100 = 408.

Average = Total Sum ÷ Count = 408 ÷ 8 = 51.

∴ The correct answer is 51.

Alternate Method

⇒ Sum = 408

⇒ Total count of prime numbers = 8

⇒ Average = 408 ÷ 8

⇒ Average = 51

∴ The correct answer is 51.

Additional Information

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. The only even prime number is 2.

Arithmetic Mean

For any set of numbers, Average = (Σx) ÷ n, where Σx is the sum of terms and n is the total number of terms.

Checking for Primes

To verify if a number N is prime, check its divisibility by prime numbers up to √N. If none divide N, then N is prime.

questions.solution: The phrase "get up on the wrong side of the bed" is an idiomatic expression that means someone is in a bad mood or acting grumpy for no apparent reason. Example: She seemed to have gotten up on the wrong side of the bed this morning, snapping at everyone around her. It suggests that a person's demeanor or disposition is negative or irritable from the moment they wake up. The phrase is often used humorously to explain someone's cranky behavior.

questions.solution: An "aerial view" refers to a perspective or visual observation of something from above, typically from an elevated position, such as an aircraft, drone, satellite, or high vantage point. Example: From the airplane window, I marveled at the breathtaking aerial view of the city below. A "bird's eye view" refers to a perspective seen from above, as if you were looking down on something from the vantage point of a bird in flight. It provides a comprehensive and often detailed view of a scene, landscape, or object. Example: Standing on the observation deck, I enjoyed a bird's eye view of the entire cityscape below.

questions.question: Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. He later tried to franchise his restaurant. B. Colonel Harland Sanders' real-life story of being disappointed numerous times in his life and still making his ambition come true late in life is truly motivating. C. He began selling chicken at the age of 40, but his dream of opening a restaurant was repeatedly denied owing to conflicts and wars. D. He is a seventh-grade dropout who tried many things in life but found them bitter.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. He later tried to franchise his restaurant.

B. Colonel Harland Sanders' real-life story of being disappointed numerous times in his life and still making his ambition come true late in life is truly motivating.

C. He began selling chicken at the age of 40, but his dream of opening a restaurant was repeatedly denied owing to conflicts and wars.

D. He is a seventh-grade dropout who tried many things in life but found them bitter.
questions.solution: Sentence B reflects on Colonel Sanders' story, emphasizing the motivational aspect of overcoming disappointments and achieving his ambition later in life. Sentence D introduces Colonel Sanders as a seventh-grade dropout who faced disappointments in various endeavors. Then, sentence C provides additional information about his life, mentioning that he began selling chicken at the age of 40 and faced repeated denials for his dream of opening a restaurant due to conflicts and wars. Finally, sentence A follows up by mentioning his attempt to franchise his restaurant, providing a continuation of his journey. The correct sequence is BDCA.

questions.question: Direction: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) In Shakespeare’s hands, English drama b) that first shone forth in his early history plays c) William Shakespeare is considered as the greatest dramatist and poet of English language. d) achieved a matchless brilliance
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

a) In Shakespeare’s hands, English drama

b) that first shone forth in his early history plays

c) William Shakespeare is considered as the greatest dramatist and poet of English language.

d) achieved a matchless brilliance
questions.solution: Sentence (c) introduces the main topic by stating that William Shakespeare is considered the greatest dramatist and poet of the English language and serves as an introductory statement about the subject. Sentence (a) continues the discussion, stating that in Shakespeare's hands, English drama achieved a matchless brilliance. Sentence (d) explains the paragraph by reiterating the idea of the brilliance achieved in English drama under Shakespeare's influence and the sequence creates a logical progression of information, offering a comprehensive view of Shakespeare's significance in English literature. Sentence (b) concludes, providing additional information about Shakespeare's early history plays, indicating a specific aspect of his work. The correct sequence is c, a, d, b. Correct sentence: William Shakespeare is considered as the greatest dramatist and poet of English language. In Shakespeare’s hands, English drama achieved a matchless brilliance that first shone forth in his early history plays.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Naïve’ from the given sentence. After years of working in politics, she had become naive and jaded, convinced that all politicians were cynical and that the system was rigged against the people.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Naïve’ from the given sentence.

After years of working in politics, she had become naive and jaded, convinced that all politicians were cynical and that the system was rigged against the people.
questions.solution: The word "Naive" means without enough experience of life and too ready to believe or trust other people. Example: I was too naive to realize what was happening. The antonym of "Naive" is "Cynical." The word "Cynical" means believing that people are motivated purely by self-interest; distrustful of human sincerity or integrity. Example: That was a cynical remark.

questions.solution: "Ironed-out" is a commonly used expression that means to resolve, smooth out, or eliminate difficulties or problems. Example: After a brief discussion, they successfully ironed-out the differences and reached a compromise. It is often used in the context of negotiations or discussions to reach an agreement or understanding. In the sentence, the phrase "ironed-out" is used metaphorically. In this context, it suggests that the driver skillfully and discreetly resolved or smoothed over the consequences of the traffic violation.
